## Why Use Decap CMS with Vite and React?

Building a static portfolio or blog with React, Vite, and Tailwind CSS offers an incredible developer experience. However, managing content by manually hardcoding JSON files or editing Markdown files directly in your IDE quickly becomes tedious.

Integrating a Git-based headless CMS like Decap CMS (formerly Netlify CMS) solves this. It gives you a clean, user-friendly UI to manage blog posts, projects, and case studies, pushing content directly to your GitHub repository without touching the codebase.

While Decap CMS works flawlessly out of the box with static site generators like Hugo or Astro, pairing it with a Single Page Application (SPA) bundler like Vite and deploying it on Vercel introduces some tricky routing and static asset issues.

Here is exactly how to architect the setup and fix the infamous blank screen and `text/html` errors.

### 1. Setting Up the Public Directory

Unlike Create React App, Vite does not bundle static files placed outside the `src` folder. Because Decap CMS runs entirely client-side via a CDN script, it needs to be served as a static HTML file, completely separate from your React routing.

To do this, you must place your admin files inside the root `public` directory. Create an `admin` folder inside `public` and add two files: `index.html` and `config.yml`.

Your directory structure should look exactly like this:

```text
├── public/
│   └── admin/
│       ├── index.html
│       └── config.yml
├── src/
├── package.json
└── vite.config.js

```

### 2. The Decap CMS HTML and Configuration

Inside `public/admin/index.html`, add the standard Decap CMS CDN script. This file serves as the entry point for the dashboard.

```html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
  <head>
    <meta charset="utf-8" />
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0" />
    <title>Content Manager</title>
  </head>
  <body>
    <!-- Decap CMS Script -->
    <script src="https://unpkg.com/decap-cms@^3.0.0/dist/decap-cms.js"></script>
  </body>
</html>

```

Next, configure your `public/admin/config.yml` to connect to your GitHub repository. This tells the CMS where to pull and push your content.

```yaml
backend:
  name: github
  repo: your-github-username/your-repo-name # e.g., 007Jamal/Bhadmus
  branch: main

media_folder: "public/uploads"
public_folder: "/uploads"

collections:
  - name: "blog"
    label: "Blog"
    folder: "src/content/blog"
    create: true
    fields:
      - { label: "Title", name: "title", widget: "string" }
      - { label: "Date", name: "date", widget: "datetime" }
      - { label: "Excerpt", name: "excerpt", widget: "text" }
      - { label: "Body", name: "body", widget: "markdown" }

```

### 3. Beating the Vite Local Development Errors

When you run your local Vite dev server (`npm run dev`) and navigate to `http://localhost:5173/admin`, you might encounter one of two frustrating errors:

**Error 1: The YAMLSyntaxError**
If you see `Response for config.yml was not yaml. (Content-Type: text/html)`, Vite is intercepting your request and serving your React `index.html` fallback instead of the YAML file.

* **The Fix:** Vite’s dev server struggles with trailing slashes. Always access your local CMS using the explicit file path: `http://localhost:5173/admin/index.html`.

**Error 2: The Blank Screen (Tracking Prevention)**
If you see a completely blank screen and a console warning stating `Tracking Prevention blocked access to storage`, your browser is blocking the `decap-cms.js` script from accessing local storage.

* **The Fix:** Click the shield or padlock icon in your browser's address bar and temporarily disable "Enhanced Tracking Protection" or allow third-party cookies for `localhost`.

### 4. The Vercel Deployment Fix (vercel.json)

When you deploy this setup to Vercel, your React app's client-side routing will hijack the `/admin` URL, causing the CMS to throw a 404 error in production.

To fix this, you need to configure Vercel's routing infrastructure. Create a `vercel.json` file at the root of your repository with these precise rewrite rules:

```json
{
  "rewrites": [
    {
      "source": "/admin",
      "destination": "/admin/index.html"
    },
    {
      "source": "/admin/(.*)",
      "destination": "/admin/index.html"
    },
    {
      "source": "/(.*)",
      "destination": "/index.html"
    }
  ]
}

```

**Why this works:** The routing logic works top-to-bottom. It tells Vercel to serve the Decap CMS static files whenever a user hits the `/admin` route first, and only falls back to your React application (`/index.html`) for the rest of your portfolio's frontend routes.

### Conclusion

By moving the CMS outside the React bundle and configuring Vercel's rewrite rules, you successfully decouple your content management from your frontend logic. You now have a fast, SEO-friendly portfolio that can be updated on the fly without running a single git command.

---

excerpt: A complete guide to integrating Decap CMS into a Vite React application. Learn how to fix local routing bugs, handle static files, and set up Vercel rewrite rules for production.
